QF.id: IV Introduction to Interest Rate Derivatives_13

question.text: A call swaption gives the holder the right to:

answer.text: Enter a swap as a fixed rate payer
Enter a swap as a fixed rate receiver
Buy a bond at a predetermined price
Sell a bond at a predetermined price

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the ETIRD workbook (p.95), a call swaption (receiver swaption) gives the holder the right to enter an interest rate swap as the fixed-rate receiver and floating-rate payer. A put swaption (payer swaption) gives the right to pay fixed and receive floating. The Trap: This naming is counterintuitive — a call swaption is about receiving fixed, not paying. The bond-buy/sell options describe bond options, not swaptions. Note: Memorize the source mapping: call = receiver (receive fixed), put = payer (pay fixed); rate-direction payoff claims need a separate citation.
